 Judgment
This appeal is filed by the 2 nd respondent in O.P.(MV) No.1022/2010 on the files of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Manjeri.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.

The petitioners in the O.P filed this claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 28.01.2010.

According to the petitioners, on 28.01.2010 at about 01.45 am, while he was travelling as a loading employee on board a lorry belonging to the 2nd respondent and driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner, the lorry capsized.
As a result of which, he fell down and sustained serious injuries.
3. The 3rd respondent is the insurer of the said lorry.

sentences.text: 4. The 3rd respondent, while admitting the valid insurance policy, contended that the injured was a gratuitous passenger on board the vehicle and hence the policy does not cover him.
It was also contended that additional premium was not collected for covering the risk of loading and unloading workers.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimonies of PWs 1 MACA NO. 1167 OF 2014 2025:KER:11461 and 2 and RW1.

The documentary evidence consists of Exts.A1 to A5 and Ext.B1.
6.
After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,48,500/- and directed respondents 1 and 2 to pay the same, after exonerating the 3rd respondent.
7. Aggrieved by the above order, the 2nd respondent/owner filed this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the Tribunal was justified in exonerating the 3rd respondent from indemnifying the compensation due to the injured.
9. Heard Sri.P.Venu Gopal, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant/owner,
Sri.K.B.Ramanand, the learned Standing Counsel for the insurance company, Sri.C.Dinesh, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and Sri.T.K.Ajith Kumar, the learned counsel appearing for the 1 st respondent/driver.
10.
According to the learned counsel for the 1st respondent, the deceased was a loading and unloading employee in the goods vehicle in which loads were transported when it met with the accident.
In order to substantiate the said contention, he has relied upon the evidence of Pws 1 and 2 and RW1.
All of them in clear terms deposed that the deceased was employed by the owner for MACA NO. 1167 OF 2014 2025:KER:11461 loading and unloading the goods transported in the said lorry.
The Tribunal, holding that there is no evidence to show that the deceased was a permanent employee of the 2nd respondent, exonerated the 3rd respondent from the liability.
11. The learned counsel for the 3rd respondent would contend that no additional premium was paid to cover the loading employees in Ext.B1 policy.
It is true that in Ext.B1 no additional premium is seen paid towards employees of the insured.

However, the learned counsel for the 1st respondent,
relying upon Section 147(1)(c) of the Motor Vehicles Act, would argue that in the case of employees there is statutory liability for the insurer, and even though no separate premium is paid for them,
the insurer is liable.

12. Section 147(1) of the M.V.Act states that:
"147. Requirements of policies and limits of liability (1) In order to comply with the requirement of this Chapter, a policy of insurance must be a policy which - Abdul Salam vs Najma V.T on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106354643/
3 (a) is issued by a person who is an authorised insurer; and (b) insures the person or classes of persons specified in the policy to the extent specified in sub-section (2) -
(i) against any liability which may be incurred by him in respect of the death of or bodily injury to any person, including owner of the goods or his authorised representative carried in the vehicles or damage to any property of a third party caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle in a public place;
(ii) against the death of or bodily injury to any passenger of a public service vehicle caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle in a public place:
MACA NO. 1167 OF 2014 2025:KER:11461 PROVIDED that a policy shall not be required - (i) to cover liability in respect of the death, arising out of and in the course of his employment, of the employer of a person insured by the policy or in respect of bodily injury sustained by such an employee arising out of and in the course of his employment other than a liability arising under the Workmen's Compensation Act,
1923 (8 of 1923) in respect of the death of, or bodily injury to, any such employee - (a) engaged in driving the vehicle, or (b) if it s a public service vehicle engaged as a conductor of the vehicle or in examining tickets on the vehicle, or (c) if it is a goods carriage, being carried in the vehicle, or (ii) to cover any contractual liability."
13.

In the decision in National Insurance Company Limited v. Mohammed Ali & Others [2012 (4)
KHC 556] in paragraph 14, a Division Bench of this Court held as follows :-
"14.

sentences.text:
Therefore a perusal of the aforesaid proviso would show that intention of the Parliament is that in order to comply with a requirement of a valid Act policy, the contract of insurance must provide for coverage in respect of death or bodily injury caused to satisfy the three categories of employees,
formulated in Clauses (a) to (c) of the proviso.

They are as follows:
1. Drivers engaged employees.
2. Conductors of a public service vehicle or person examined as ticket examiner.

4 3.

sentences.text: any person carried on a goods carriage.

While it is true that the definition of a goods carriage as contained in the Motor Vehicles Act is such that it does not contemplate carrying any person, the words employed in Cl.(c) of the proviso does not leave us in any doubt that as far as the liability under the Workmen's Compensation Act is concerned with which the proviso is concerned, Parliament contemplates employees who may be travelling MACA NO. 1167 OF 2014 2025:KER:11461 in a goods carriage.
We are unable to limit the benefit of the proviso to only the driver or to the conductor/ticket examiner.
If the arguments of the appellant were accepted that only the driver and conductor, ticket examiner, are to be comprehended within the proviso there was no need at all to frame Cl.(c).
Also the very fact that the Legislature used the words "or persons carried on a goods vehicle" itself shows that it is intended to cover not the driver but somebody other than the driver.
No doubt he must be an employee.
This interpretation which we have placed does not go contrary to the dictum laid down by the Apex Court in any of the decisions cited before us.

The distinction in regard to the insurer's liability under the Workmen's Compensation Act has been succinctly brought out in decision of the Apex Court itself which we have adverted/extracted [paragraph 12 of the decision reported in 2007(2) KLT 219 Supreme Court, 2007 KHC 3231 : JT 2007 (4) SC 28 : AIR 2007 SC 1334 : 2007 (9) SCC 486 (supra)]."

14. In the decision in Oriental Insurance Company Limited v. Velayudhan and Others, 2003(1)KLT 592, another Division Bench of this court also held that the loading and unloading worker of a goods vehicle will be statutorily covered under clause (c) of the first proviso to Section 147(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act.

in which,

sentences.text: Therefore, now the question to be considered is whether the deceased was the loading and unloading worker in the aforesaid lorry.

In the instant case, from the evidence of PWs 1, 2 and RW1,
it is revealed that the deceased was employed by the owner for loading and unloading the goods transported in the said vehicle.
It is also corroborated by the fact that at the time of the accident,
logs were transported in the said vehicle

. Therefore, there is clear evidence to show that the deceased was an employee of the owner, coming within the sweep of "any person carried on a goods carriage" and as such, in the light of clause (c) to the first proviso to Section 147(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation due to his legal representatives, as provided under the Schedule to the Employees Compensation Act.

For the very same reasons, the order of the Tribunal mulcting the 1 st respondent with the liability to pay the compensation is liable to be set aside and the 3 rd respondent will be held responsible to pay the same.

sentences.text: As per Section 4 of the Employees Compensation Act, the amount of compensation payable in case of death is an amount equal to 50% of monthly wages of the deceased employee multiplied by the relevant factor.
Since the deceased was aged 29 years, the relevant factor is 209.92 as seen from Schedule IV to the Employees Compensation Act.
18. The petitioners claim is that the deceased was getting a monthly MACA NO. 1167 OF 2014 2025:KER:11461 income of Rs,10,000/-.
However, the petitioner could not prove the income of the deceased as claimed in the claim petition.
However, the Tribunal fixed the notional income of the deceased at RS.3,750/- only.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie during the year 2010 will come to Rs.7,500/-.

Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the notional income of the deceased is fixed as that of a coolie at Rs.7,500/-.
Therefore, compensation payable under Section 147(1)(c) of the Motor Vehicles Act, will come to Rs.7,87,200/- (3,750 x 209.92).
For the said amount, they are also entitled to get interest at the rate of 9% per anum.

19. The learned counsel for the 3 rd respondent would argue that in this case, the claimants have not filed any cross-objection and as such the compensation awarded by the Tribunal cannot be enhanced.

However, the law is well settled that in proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act, the duty of the Tribunals and Courts is to award just and reasonable compensation to the victims, and for the said purpose, there is nothing wrong in ordering enhancement of compensation even in an appeal filed by the insurer or any of the respondents.

20. In the result, this appeal is disposed of directing the 3 rd respondent to pay a sum of Rs.7,87,200/- (Rupees Seven Lakh Eighty Seven Thousand Two Hundred Only) to the claimants,
less the amount already paid/deposited, if any, MACA NO. 1167 OF 2014 2025:KER:11461 along with interest @ 9% per annum, excluding interest for a period of 316 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs,
within a period of two months from today.
21. On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE SMA.
